meaning: Pay an employer gives the person for work as an employee: salary, hourly wages, tips, commissions, bonuses, overtime, paid leave and military basic pay; not pay another kind names.

Special pay from a uniformed service for hazardous or combat duty: hostile fire or imminent danger pay under 37 U.S.C. 310, and other pay received because the member is deployed to a designated combat zone (combat_zone).
Pay for work under a federal or State work-study program for students.
Wages for on-the-job training under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act.
Wages from a summer youth employment and training program.
Wages for community service employment under the Senior Community Service Employment Program (Title V of the Older Americans Act).
Wages from subsidized employment other than WIOA on-the-job training: an apprenticeship, on-the-job training or a transitional job whose wages a public program subsidizes.
Wages the U.S. Census Bureau paid for temporary employment related to the decennial Census.

A Difficulty of Care payment: compensation for live-in home care of a person who qualifies for foster care or a Home and Community Based Services waiver, needed because of that person's physical, mental or emotional handicap (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.1).

The value of goods, shelter, housing or services (not money) the person received in place of cash as compensation for work, as an employee or in self-employment: the value the payer supplies or the person declares, or the current market value where none is given.

Money an employer paid to a third party for an expense of the person's household (rent, utilities, a bill), as part of the person's compensation, from funds the employer would otherwise pay the person.
Money an employer paid directly to the person, recurring or not, to help the person buy private health insurance; not a premium the employer pays to the insurer.

Gross receipts, capital gains included, of a business, trade or profession the person carries on as sole proprietor, partner, independent contractor or consultant, other than a farm (farm_self_employment_receipts) and boarders (boarder_payments).
Gross receipts of a farm the person operates on the person's own account, as owner, renter or tenant: the value of the products sold and the other receipts of the farm.

Payments from persons who pay to live, or to take regular meals, in the person's home (provides), contributions toward the home's shelter expenses included; not an amount a boarder pays directly to someone outside the home, not rent from property the person does not live in, and not the receipts of a commercial boarding house (self_employment_receipts).

A cost of doing business no other cost kind names, paid for the person's self-employment: rent of business premises, wholesale cost of merchandise, stock, raw materials, seed and fertilizer, utilities, taxes on the business or its property, labor, insurance and upkeep of necessary equipment.
Interest paid on a loan for the business or to buy income-producing property.
Payments on the principal of the purchase price of, or of a loan for, income-producing real estate, capital assets, equipment, machinery or other durable goods.
Depreciation of the business's equipment or property as its books or tax return state it.
The cost of the room or space in the person's home used for the business.
The cost of using a vehicle for the business (mileage for business purposes only).
The documented cost of providing the room or meals that boarders pay for (boarder_payments).
Social Security (title II) benefits: retirement, survivors' or disability insurance, on the person's own record or another's; not a refund of Medicare premiums (medicare_premium_refund).
Supplemental Security Income paid by the Social Security Administration (title XVI).

A pension, annuity or retirement benefit from a former employer, a union, the military or a government retirement system, Railroad Retirement included; not a distribution from an account the person owns (savings_account_distribution).
Unemployment insurance benefits paid by a State or the federal government.

Current child support paid for a child, other than arrears, stated on the list of the child it is paid for, whoever receives it on the child's behalf (a parent or caretaker, the payee); see the precision.
Child support paid toward support owed for months before the month received, stated on the list of the child it is paid for, as child_support is.
Colorado Works (TANF) basic cash assistance.
An Adult Financial grant payment: Old Age Pension, Aid to the Needy Disabled or Aid to the Blind, other than the Home Care Allowance (home_care_allowance).
Interest that is exempt from federal income tax, such as interest on municipal bonds.
Taxable interest and dividends: the return paid on money or securities the person holds.
Rent or royalties from property the person owns and does not actively manage as a business.
Workers' compensation benefits for a work injury or illness, an award's amounts for the claim's expenses included (see claim_expense).
Winnings from a lottery or any other game of chance, one record per game.
Money the person obtained by selling or converting a personal resource the person owned.

Grants, scholarships, fellowships and educational loans for the cost of education or training, other than a training allowance from a workforce program, other than benefits paid only on condition of school attendance (school_attendance_conditional_benefit) and other than student financial assistance under Title IV of the Higher Education Act or from a Bureau of Indian Education program (title_iv_or_bie_student_aid).
The proceeds of a bona fide loan the person must repay, a reverse mortgage excepted.
A reimbursement of expenses the person paid or will pay, which is not a gain to the person.
Home energy assistance under federal law: LEAP (LIHEAP) or other federally funded assistance with energy costs.
Home energy assistance not under federal law, from a nonprofit organization or the energy supplier.
An income tax refund, rebate or credit, the earned income tax credit and Colorado's Property Tax/Rent/Heat credit included.
A public agency's refund of taxes paid on real property or on food (one class, 20 CFR 416.1124(c)(1)), other than an income tax refund or credit.

A payment a federal statute excludes from income for federally funded means-tested programs (the list in the federally excluded payments fact), other than a Domestic Volunteer Service Act Title I volunteer payment.
A payment to a volunteer under Title I of the Domestic Volunteer Service Act (VISTA, University Year for Action, Urban Crime Prevention), below the minimum wage.

Compensation paid to the person as a victim of crime under the Colorado Crime Victim Compensation Act or a like program.
A payment to the person as a foster care provider for a child placed in the person's home.
A kinship care payment to the person for a related child in the person's care.

Refugee resettlement funds or reception and placement money from a resettlement agency, or the Interim Cash Payment of the Colorado Refugee Services Program; not Refugee Cash Assistance.
A living allowance, stipend or education award paid for service in AmeriCorps (national service under the National and Community Service Act).

A payment from the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (other income or supportive services) or a youth employment and training project (YIEPP, YCCIP, YETP), other than a training allowance from another program and other than a payment from WIOA's employment and training activities for adults and dislocated workers under 29 U.S.C. 3174 (wioa_adult_or_dislocated_worker_payment).

A training allowance from a vocational or rehabilitation program other than WIOA and the youth projects (a JOBS or vocational rehabilitation allowance, for example), to the extent it is not a reimbursement.
General Assistance granted by a county department, before or as a supplement to other assistance.
Emergency assistance received on a one-time basis from a county department or another agency or organization, other than home energy assistance and major disaster or emergency assistance.

A personal care or home care allowance from a federal, State or local government program to purchase in-home supportive services for the person, other than the Adult Financial Home Care Allowance (home_care_allowance).

The Adult Financial Home Care Allowance paid to the client (9 CCR 2503-5 3.500), its own kind so a rule can read it apart from the Old Age Pension and Aid to the Needy Disabled grants (coverage review 3 of Adult Financial, H-5).
VA Aid and Attendance or housebound allowance (see used_for_uncovered_medical_care).
A State's annuity for a blind, disabled or aged veteran.
Cash a charitable organization gave the person on the basis of need, other than a gift for a life-threatening condition.
A cash gift (or an in-kind gift converted to cash) from a 501(c)(3) organization to or for the person because the person has a life-threatening condition.
Money a person outside the household gave the person, with no obligation to repay and not for work, other than a gift from a charitable organization.
Money a non-citizen received from a sponsor, or a sponsor's spouse, who does not live with the non-citizen.
Emergency assistance paid to a migrant or seasonal farmworker in the job stream.
